To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the primary tumors and their metastatic foci differ from each other in their growth rate and intensity of DNA synthesis.
the growth rate of the primary tumour and the metastatic lymph nodes is different and the intensity of the DNA-synthesis in these two types of tumour tissue is different as well.
the growth rate of transplanted primary tumors was 0.3-0.5 mm/day and that the incorporation of thymidine into tumor cells was 0.5-0.7%/day.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of the kinetics of tumor growth and its metastasis.
the possibility of the application of the kinetic method to study the development of experimental tumors and their metastatic spread.
the possibility of the use of the kinetic characteristics of DNA synthesis in the primary and metastatic tumor cells for evaluation of the degree of the metastatic process development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of the growth process is a more significant characteristic of the tumor development than the intensity of DNA synthesis.

the metastasis of tumors is a process of a complex and multifaceted nature, which can be characterized by the rate of tumor growth, intensity of its DNA synthesis, and the number of cells with labelled thymidine.

metastasizing tumors, in comparison with the primary ones, are characterized by a higher intensity of the DNA biosynthesis and a more active incorporation of the labelled thymidine, which is accompanied by a higher rate of the process of the tumor development and a more rapid incorporation of the labelled substance into the cells of the tumor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

metastasis of Walker carcinosarcomas and Zajdela hepatomas in the lymph nodes is a complex process, the development of which is determined by many factors, among them the rate of the primary tumor growth and its intensity of DNA synthesis.
the rate of the growth of primary tumor and the intensity of the DNA-synthesis are not directly correlated with the number of metastases and the rate of the metastasis formation.
metastasizing tumors are more active than primary tumors, and the metastases are more active than the primary tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the process of tumor metastasis is a complex multistage phenomenon, and the rate of the metastasis process is determined not only by the rate of the primary tumor growth but also by the intensity of the DNA biosynthesis and number of proliferating cells in the tumor.
metastases of the Walker carcinosarcomas are characterized by a more intensive DNA synthesis than those of the ascites hepatoma.
the process of metastasis is not only a result of the growth of primary tumor, but it has its own peculiarities.
